source.author: verg
source.text: Non haec sollemnia nobis, has ex more dapes, hanc tanti numinis aram vana superstitio veterumque ignara deorum inposuit: saevis, hospes Troiane, periclis servati facimus meritosque novamus honores.
source.text_original: 'Non haec sollemnia nobis, / has ex more dapes, hanc tanti numinis aram / vana superstitio veterumque ignara deorum / inposuit: saevis, hospes Troiane, periclis / servati facimus meritosque novamus honores.
source.text_english: It is not vain superstition, nor ignorance of the ancient gods, that has imposed on us these rites, these customary feasts, this altar of so great a divinity: saved from savage perils, we perform them, Trojan guest, and renew the honors duly owed.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: unde Vergilius: uana superstitio ueterumque ignara deorum.
reuse.text_original: unde Vergilius: uana superstitio ueterumque ignara deorum.
reuse.text_english: Hence Virgil says: vain superstition, and ignorant of the gods of old.
